replies.author: Trashy_io
replies.body: I'll agree it's a helpful learning process but thats about it, very much so in this sub as Ill bet everyone in here has done at minimum one. Just wish there was more self governance in terms of what is posted in this sub thats all. If you aren't doing something unique or useful then the post is noise. I don't want to discourage anyone from posting or participating but instead motivate themselves to push farther before posting. And add some in-site in your post on a related topic to your game. replies.author: bloodwolftico
replies.body:
I just found your game page. I think it looks pretty cool! I'd like to watch a trailer with actual ingame audio tho so I can measure how the game feels a bit more.

  
I wasnt able to find any reviews tho, but was curious what you'd put under the AI disclaimer:

*The game has used chatgpt's image model with no artist prompts used. The game uses udio for the music.*

  
So when you saw "no artist prompts used" what did you mean? Like, you didnt mention anyone regarding style? Example: make X picture like Studio Ghibli. Also, typo at the end for "audio for the music" (you skipped the "A"). 

  
Curious about a couple more things if that's ok;

1- Did you use [Suno.ai](http://Suno.ai) or a different audio source?

2- How large is your team? I can see you've been working on this for a while.

3- How did you create your in-game sounds?

4- Did you use ChatGPT image creation for all sprites?

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body:
That's my newest game Vinegar Mutter, it's not out yet , it's a lot further along then what the trailer shows. I was referring to my game Mekkablood which is released.

It's just me solo developed, the sounds aren't ai, but the music is suno. I used a professional voice actor for the voices, and yes I used chatgpt for all of the sprites and didn't reference any artist in the prompts.

comments.author: ParadisePrime
comments.body:
I avoided going all-in on AI for a while and mainly used it for advice or coding help, while still implementing everything myself. Then I finally said fuck it and downloaded Codex, and by the Nine, my productivity skyrocketed. It’s insane how well it understands what I’m trying to say, and even when it misses, I can usually just prompt it again and it gets it right.

I’m flying through things now.

replies.author: sharkymcstevenson2
replies.body: Preach! It’s so fun to work with too

replies.author: ParadisePrime
replies.body:
Exactly. Thankfully I just started a new job and will be trying out the Pro version to see if it's worth it, but the Plus version is doing great already.

I used Claude for a bit but the usage window is so small and  it kinda doesn't understand context very well. It's ironically missing the human understanding and basically requires Chatgpt to convert my intentions into better prompts for it in my experience.
